title: Forces
seo_title: Year 7 Science: Forces Worksheets (Resultant Force, Weight and Mass, Springs)
standard_text: Forces as pushes or pulls, arising from the interaction between two objects; using force arrows in diagrams, adding forces in one dimension, balanced and unbalanced forces; moment as the turning effect of a force; forces: associated with deforming objects; stretching and squashing – springs; with rubbing and friction between surfaces, with pushing things out of the way; resistance to motion of air and water; forces measured in newtons, measurements of stretch or compression as force is changed; force-extension linear relation; non-contact forces: gravity forces acting at a distance on Earth and in space; weight = mass × gravitational field strength.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 science worksheets on forces: types of force, force arrows, resultant force, balanced and unbalanced forces, weight and mass, and stretching springs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Forces are pushes or pulls, measured in newtons.
key_sub: Resultant force decides how motion changes. Weight = mass × g.
body_html:
How to think about it

A force is a push or a pull, measured in newtons (N).

  • Add forces in the same direction; subtract opposite ones. The answer is the resultant force.
  • Balanced forces: no change in motion. Unbalanced forces: speeding up, slowing down or turning.
  • Weight = mass × g. On Earth g ≈ 10 N/kg. Mass does not change; weight does.
Example

30 N right, 12 N left. Resultant?

30 − 12

Answer: 18 N to the right

Example

Weight of 5 kg on Earth?

5 × 10

Answer: 50 N

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a moving object needs a resultant force to keep moving.
  • Thinking mass and weight are the same.
  • Adding forces that point in opposite directions.

faq.q: How do you find the resultant force?
faq.a: Add forces acting in the same direction and subtract forces acting in opposite directions. The resultant points the way of the bigger total.

faq.q: What happens when forces are balanced?
faq.a: The motion does not change: a still object stays still and a moving object keeps moving at the same speed in the same direction.

faq.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
faq.a: Mass (kg) is the amount of matter and is the same everywhere. Weight (N) is the pull of gravity: weight = mass × g, which is about 10 N/kg on Earth.
